overview: The Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida has an area inside Everglades National Park, called the Miccosukee Reserved Area, set aside for its use under a 1998 law. This bill expands that area to include Osceola Camp, a community within the park shown on a 2023 National Park Service map. It also requires the Interior Department, working with the tribe, to take steps within two years to protect the structures at Osceola Camp from flooding. As of October 28, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate's calendar, meaning it is eligible for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say the camp's residents have long lived on this land, and bringing it into the reserved area and protecting homes from flooding addresses a clear need for the tribe.
against: Critics say moving national park land into the reserved area reduces the part of the park under direct Park Service management, and flood-protection work could affect the surrounding Everglades.
